compiled_state.title: As a DSO maintainer, I can run a one-shot backfill to classify the last 60 days of closed bugs so that historical data has classification coverage
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Create a one-shot backfill script that applies the same bug-classifier-haiku agent to all closed bugs in the prior 60-day window.
**Why**: SC4 ensures historical data is not lost. Without the backfill, stats from SC5 are biased toward only post-ship bugs; SC6 self-use requires backfill to run during the sprint as end-to-end proof of the classification pipeline.
**Scope**:
- IN: plugins/dso/scripts/backfill-bug-types.sh; .claude/locks/ directory creation; single-run lock contract
- OUT: The classifier agent (owned by S2); the ongoing closure-time dispatch (owned by S2 and S6)
- Note: Per epic spec, this story is deferred-ok if it complicates registry + Phase G + retro delivery.

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, plugins/dso/scripts/backfill-bug-types.sh exists and iterates all bug tickets closed in the prior 60 days, using ticket list --type=bug (excludes deleted tickets)
  <- Satisfies: "SC4: Backfill script iterates all bug tickets closed in the prior 60 days"
- When this story is complete, backfill MUST invoke the bug-classifier-haiku agent defined by S2 — it MUST NOT re-implement classification logic; failure-marker fallback (bug-type-uncategorized + bug-type-classifier-failed-<reason>) is identical to S2's dispatch path
  <- Satisfies: "SC4: same classifier" (adversarial finding: explicit classifier contract)
- When this story is complete, backfill creates .claude/locks/ directory if missing (mkdir -p); uses lock file .claude/locks/backfill-bug-types.lock containing PID and ISO-8601 start timestamp; on lock-detected exits 0 with an informational message (not error); lock is removed on both success and failure via trap on EXIT; the lock is REPO_ROOT-anchored to prevent concurrent worktree runs from bypassing it
  <- Satisfies: "SC4: uses a single-run lock under .claude/locks/" (adversarial finding: lockdir contract)
- When this story is complete, backfill is idempotent: re-run skips tickets already carrying any bug-type-* tag; empty-list is a graceful no-op with exit 0
  <- Satisfies: "SC4: idempotent re-run skips tickets already carrying any bug-type-* tag"
- When this story is complete, post-run, every closed bug in the 60-day window carries exactly one bug-type-* tag (the classifier-failed co-tag does not count toward the one-tag-per-bug rule)
  <- Satisfies: "SC4: post-run, every closed bug in the 60-day window carries exactly one bug-type-* tag"
- When this story is complete, backfill uses additive tagging (ticket tag <id> bug-type-<slug>) and MUST NOT touch unrelated tags including CLI_user (autonomous classification must not mutate user-provenance tags)
  <- Satisfies: adversarial finding on CLI_user tag semantics
- When this story is complete, unit tests are written and passing for all new or modified logic

## Considerations

- [Correctness] Backfill is autonomous — must NOT mutate CLI_user tags on historical tickets. Use additive ticket-tag calls only; never call ticket untag or batch-replace the full tag set.
- [Performance] 60-day window may iterate many tickets. Ensure empty-list is a graceful no-op and the script terminates cleanly without hanging on zero results.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
